$comment: One output shape for every check command's JSON report, across every role. Issue #1174. Check commands already share the 0/1/2 (satisfied/violated/indeterminate) exit convention; this is the JSON body behind that exit so Advisor and Launcher can render status uniformly, and in plain language, across roles they did not author. The canonical TypeScript shape and constructor live in packages/controller/src/envelope.ts (`buildCheckOutputEnvelope`, `envelopeToExitCode`); how a package adopts them is the `adoption` rule below (issue #1384).

fieldShapes.package: string -- the exact published package name that produced this report
fieldShapes.version: string -- exact semver of the package version that produced this report
fieldShapes.verdict: one of `verdicts`, and MUST match the process's own 0/1/2 exit exactly as gateResultToExitCode already folds it (packages/controller/src/gates/result.ts)
fieldShapes.summary: string -- exactly one sentence, plain language, written for a non-technical client to read with no other context
fieldShapes.findings: CheckFinding[] -- may be empty only when verdict is "satisfied"
fieldShapes.metric: optional { name: string, value: number, direction: "increase" | "decrease" | "maintain" | "target-range" } -- present only when this check owns a measured metric
fieldShapes.nextAction: optional string -- one sentence naming the single next accountable step, when the verdict is not "satisfied"

findingShape.rule: string -- stable machine id for this exact finding kind
findingShape.message: string -- human-readable, names what is wrong
findingShape.path: optional string -- the file or field the finding is about

adoption.rule: No package hand-writes a second definition of this shape. A package that depends on @clossys/controller imports `buildCheckOutputEnvelope` from it. A package with no runtime dependencies carries a GENERATED copy at src/generated/check-output-envelope.ts, produced by scripts/sync-envelope-copies.mjs from the canonical source (the one transform: `GateVerdict` is inlined from packages/controller/src/gates/result.ts), and never edits it: a copy that differs by one byte from what the generator produces now is a finding in report mode and --enforce alike.
adoption.evidence: Adoption is shown by the package's own shipped source (src/, tests excluded) calling `buildCheckOutputEnvelope` imported from @clossys/controller, from the canonical module itself, or from a current generated copy -- the constructor enforces this contract's hard rules at construction time. A hand-written sample document (the former packages/<pkg>/check-output-envelope.fixture.json convention) is reported `sample-only` and is never accepted as adoption: it proves the shape can be typed, not that the package emits it. Graded by scripts/check-package-conformance.mjs item 2, report mode first.

alternativesRejected.zero-dependency packages take a runtime: breaks the zero-dependency install those packages promise, for a handful of types and one small function
alternativesRejected.a separate published envelope-only packa: a new package to version, qualify, and publish for one file; a generated, drift-checked copy gives the same single source with no new release surface
alternativesRejected.keep accepting a sample file: passes a package that emits nothing

adoption.migration: Existing hand-written local shapes (for example packages/designer/src/tokens/identity-checks.ts's IdentityVerdict / IdentityFinding) convert in each package's own lane, not in the change that set this rule.

rule: `summary` is always exactly one sentence in plain language; it is the ONLY field Advisor and Launcher may show a non-technical client without translation. `findings` is non-empty whenever `verdict` is "violated" or "indeterminate" -- a non-satisfied verdict with no findings is itself malformed, because it reports a problem while refusing to say what it is. `metric`, when present, uses the same `direction` vocabulary docs/contracts/role-loop-archetypes.json already declares (`metricVocabulary.directions`).
